text: A useful app is not automatically a patentable invention.

Section 3(k) has four separate exclusions: mathematical methods, business methods, algorithms, and computer programs per se. Passing one test does not establish that the entire invention is patentable.
Abstract math and algorithm steps remain excluded. The document distinguishes these from enabled technical implementations in which the math or steps serve a larger technical process.
Explain how it works, not just what it promises. Describe the components, connections, steps, implementation and best method known to you.

AI disclosure follows the actual inventive contribution. If the innovation is the learning implementation, explain the architecture and training. If it is the data pipeline, explain that pipeline and why it produces the technical result.

Human inventorship matters in the document's AI treatment. It treats autonomous or very limited human-intervention AI-generated inventions as non-patentable because AI cannot be the person claiming true and first inventorship. AI-assisted human inventions are not categorically excluded.

AI / ML / DL: Artificial intelligence is the broad field; machine learning learns behavior from data; deep learning uses multi-layer neural networks. A model is the trained or trainable mechanism that maps inputs to outputs.
Architecture, layer, activation and parameters: Architecture is how the model is organized; layers are successive processing stages; activations are rules applied within those stages;
Attention, embeddings and temporal processing: Attention weights relevant input information; embeddings are numerical representations; temporal processing tracks patterns over time.

Preprocessing, segmentation and NDVI: Preprocessing prepares raw data; segmentation divides an image into relevant regions; the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index is a calculated indicator of vegetation. Atmospheric correction adjusts satellite observations for atmospheric effects.

Accuracy, recall, false positive and false negative: Accuracy counts correct predictions overall; recall asks how many actual positive cases were found; a false positive incorrectly flags a case; a false negative misses one. Robustness means maintaining the intended behavior under the relevant variations.

1. Understand the claims and the boundaries they define. 2. Identify relevant earlier disclosures: public disclosures, publications, patents and patent applications. 3. Compare the relevant technical details, documenting similarities and differences. 4. Check both explicit disclosure and implicit disclosure of the same invention. 5. Identify material differences across the entire claimed scope. 6. Assess the claimed combination as a whole, not merely whether its individual elements were known.
7. Record the conclusion with the specific prior-art passages and reasons supporting it.
Novelty alone is insufficient. The invention as a whole must satisfy the statutory technical-advance/economic-significance requirement and non-obviousness.

1. Identify the relevant skilled person: a competent craftsman or engineer. 2. Establish that person's common general knowledge at the priority date. 3. Identify the claim's inventive concept, or interpret the claim to determine it. 4. Identify differences between the prior art/state of the art and that concept. 5. Without hindsight, decide whether those differences were obvious or required inventive ingenuity.

5.3 Industrial applicability: can it actually be used? The invention must be capable of being made or used in industry. It must be workable and useful; the description and common general knowledge must make a practical use and concrete benefit apparent. Speculation about a future use or a vague objective is insufficient.
Faster internal computation: Innovative implemented algorithms or architecture interactions improve processor computation.
Faster storage access: Improved caching or disk input/output scheduling reduces access time. Example: explain a caching mechanism and how it cuts storage reads. - F

Ordinary automation: Manual record keeping or scheduling moved to a computer, without an additional technical gain beyond its inherent operation.

Standard retrieval/lookup: No technical improvement beyond normal querying. Examples: standard keyword matching; basic library catalog queries. The original row also repeats playlist language; its distinct substance is preserved here. [Source p. 43; Table 2]
Preference-only personalization: Recommendations based only on preferences/history without technical system effect.

Algorithm, p. 46: Identify the steps. Abstract steps missing implementation details are excluded. Enabled technical steps that produce a technical solution to a real-world problem avoid this exclusion; otherwise excluded.

Computer program per se, pp. 47-48: Interpret the whole claim, identify essential technical features and the core problem/solution, then assess technical character and effect. The chart's yes branch avoids this exclusion. The accompanying prose on p. 35 specifies that the effect must go beyond an incidental effect.

separates AI-generated inventions, created autonomously or with very limited human intervention, from AI-assisted inventions, where AI is a tool used in the inventive process. It says the former are not patentable because AI cannot be the “person” claiming true and first inventorship under section 6. It says the latter are not categorically excluded under 3(k), provided they meet patentability criteria and show technical effect through tangible inventive applications.

The specification named black-box modernization, distributed-object technology, middleware, object-oriented techniques and familiar devices, but did not teach how they actually produced the claimed integration. Collecting ideas from patent/non-patent literature did not supply the missing implementation.

Explain how the transformation occurs using the known processes and variables, sufficiently specifically for a skilled reader to reproduce it. Where test results/evidence validate output accuracy, include them, especially for precision-critical uses.

Identify the training data and its distinctive characteristics, explain why they fit the technical problem, describe the model and training methodology, and show predictable/reliable technical results. The disclosure includes relevant hyperparameters, optimization, training duration and preprocessing, not merely the statement “use a trained model.”
Disclose every material preprocessing step/function and its connection to the final model. Missing the connection between raw inputs and prepared learning data can fail enablement.

Explain the agent's observation and influence on its environment, states, available actions and rewards/feedback values. Omitting essential details that a skilled reader cannot deduce can make the disclosure non-enabled.
Explain interaction with hardware/system architecture and how internal storage, scheduling or processing metrics improve.
Disclose essential dataset traits unless a skilled reader can identify them without undue experimentation. Include relevant domain, diversity, precise labelling and unique characteristics.

If the inventive contribution is a new learning implementation, fully explain its unique elements, mathematical basis and operational steps. If the contribution is innovative creation, curation or use of data that makes a known algorithm achieve the result, focus disclosure on that data process.

Prompt or workflow design: Identify whether the contribution is instructions, a mental/business process or information organization, or an enabled technical solution. A useful answer produced by an ordinary workflow does not itself prove the required technical effect.
RAG/search/memory: Distinguish ordinary lookup/personalization from implemented improvements in indexing, storage access, memory utilization or retrieval performance.
Fine-tuning or dataset selection: Identify whether the claimed contribution lies in model implementation, essential dataset traits or data curation.

Agents and tool control: Explain environment interaction, observations, actions and feedback when reinforcement learning is involved; explain actual control interfaces for physical/network systems. Illustration: an agent controlling signals must teach how decisions reach the actuators, - A

Architecture claims: Explain connections, operational steps and the specific technical effect. Illustration: a block diagram containing “memory,” “reasoning” and “learning” boxes is insufficient if it does not teach the claimed mechanism. [Derived illustration; source pp. 21-23, 50-53]
No dedicated framework label changes the need for novelty, non-obviousness, industrial applicability, enablement and applicable exclusion checks.
